Definition: the shrine or innermost part of the sanctuary
BiblicalUsage: The innermost part of the sanctuary is the holy of holies, where the ark rested beneath the wings of the cherubim. Solomon built the oracle within the temple, overlaid it with pure gold, and set the ark there, and the psalmist lifts his hands toward it in prayer. It is the place where God dwells between the cherubim, and no one enters but the high priest, once a year, with blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the inner shrine is the heart of the temple and the heart of the gospel: the place where God meets man was once shut, and Christ has opened it. I hold that the veil is torn, and the way into the holiest is now open to all who come by His blood.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
